h1: Mango pre-flowering: what dealers should plan in the next 15 days
title: Mango pre-flowering: dealer plan for the next 15 days | GBO
desc: With mango flowering weeks away in western India: how dealers and co-ops can stage stock, audit the godown and brief growers without promising results.
answer: Plan for a moving date, not a fixed one. Split mango stock into tranches released by orchard stage, check every biostimulant against the current Schedule VI list, brief counter staff on panicle, bloom and fruit set, and tell growers that flowering depends on cool weather, shoot maturity and tree load. Promise nothing.
sections: flowering-date-risk
The flowering date is your main stock risk

Mango flowering does not keep to a calendar. At Navsari Agricultural University's Paria station in Valsad, a two-season study of Alphonso and Kesar recorded flowering from the first week of December in one year and from January in the next. That is about a month's difference in demand at one site.

The Konkan shows the same problem. A Dr Balasaheb Sawant Konkan Krishi Vidyapeeth paper says flowering there commences in November. It also says that since 2006, delayed rains, overcast skies, heat and humidity in September and October have often produced vegetative shoots instead. Such a flush needs another 80 to 100 days to mature. On that figure, a shoot flushing in early November may not be ready before late January. A 2025 Junagadh Agricultural University paper on Kesar also says flowering is often delayed by post-monsoon flushes.

Three things drive the date. A 2022 paper in Plants notes that most cultivars flower only after cool temperatures, and that a heavy fruit load in summer can inhibit flower induction the next winter. A review of mango reproductive physiology adds that stems need a rest period, and that in the tropics the age of the last flush is the dominant factor.

So a dealer's real question is not "when is flowering?" It is "how much of my territory has mature shoots, and how much has a fresh flush?"
next-15-days
What to settle in the next 15 days

DaysJobWhat you should have at the end
1 to 3Ask field staff and your largest growers what the shoots look like, block by block.A rough split of your territory: mature shoots, recent flush, buds swelling.
4 to 6Audit the godown. Match each biostimulant to the current list and its paperwork.A saleable list and a held list.
7 to 9Agree tranches with suppliers: a small first lot, then a reorder triggered by panicles seen.A dated reorder rule, not a single order.
10 to 12Brief counter staff on the stages and the phrases below.One shared script across shops and field staff.
13 to 15Set a weekly review using local weather and university bulletins.A named person who calls the release of the next tranche.

Use free public signals for that weekly review. University agromet bulletins are one. The Navsari bulletin for 2 to 6 November 2024, issued by the university and the India Meteorological Department, already carried a mango hopper line. In the Konkan, Dr BSKKV's 2023 recommendations include a weather-based model for predicting vegetative flush in Alphonso. Agronomists serving that belt should read it.
what-stock
What stock to plan, by job rather than by label

DemandWhen it tends to comePlanning note
Boron and zincPre-flowering, where a test or symptoms point to a shortageSell against a soil or leaf test where you can. Avoid stocking for blanket use.
Seaweed extract and amino acidsPanicle to fruit setHold this for the second tranche. A late flush can push the need out by weeks.
Crop protection for hopper and mildewFrom early panicleOnly if you hold the right licence. Follow university advice for product and dose.
Humic acid and biofertilisersMainly after harvestOur mango stage table places these after harvest. Do not push them now as a flowering product.

Be honest about the evidence. On micronutrients, the Junagadh trial on Kesar tested foliar sprays during flowering over two seasons, including boric acid and a micronutrient mixture, alone and with growth regulators. Its best yield and return came from a growth regulator with micronutrients. It did not include seaweed.

On seaweed, a study at Bhubaneswar reported better fruit retention in mango with an Ascophyllum nodosum extract than in untreated trees, in one season's fieldwork. Trials on Kesar at Navsari found that the response to seaweed extract changed with the pH of the spray solution. That is a useful point for your agronomists: mixing water matters. Neither study is a promise for any product, season or orchard.
godown-check
Check the godown against the current list

This matters more this season than it did before 2025. According to a Press Information Bureau release of 9 September 2025, S.O. 882(E) of 23 February 2021 brought biostimulants under the Fertiliser Control Order. Provisional certificates (G3) went to more than 8,000 products. Those registrations stand invalid since 17 June 2025. As of September 2025, Schedule VI listed 146 biostimulant products.

That count is dated, and the list can change by amendment, so check the latest Gazette list before you buy. The release does not say what happens to stock made under an old certificate. Do not guess. Hold doubtful lots and get an answer in writing. Our Schedule VI page and label and documents checklist can help you prepare the questions. Rules and their local application vary, so check with your state agriculture department.
stages-to-talk-about
Which stages to talk about

StageWhat official or research sources sayYour talking point
Shoot maturityStems need rest; a late flush delays flowering (see above)."Let us look at your shoots before we discuss anything else."
Early panicleA national IPM bulletin ties the first hopper spray to early panicle formation. At Paria, powdery mildew symptoms were noticed from panicle initiation."Start scouting now. Ask your university or KVK what to apply."
Flower openingThe same bulletin says insecticides and fungicides should be avoided during flower opening or pollination. It also advises keeping pollinators in the orchard. An ICAR-IIHR study on Alphonso at Bengaluru found lower fruit set when insects were excluded, and a blowfly did as well as a wild bee."Protect the insects doing the pollination."
Fruit setAt Paria, mildew severity was highest in weeks 11 and 12, mid to late March, at flowering cum fruit set. It related negatively to humidity and positively to temperature and evaporation. The Junagadh paper notes each panicle bears 5,000 to 6,000 flowers and only about 0.01% mature into fruit."Most flowers will never become fruit. That is normal."

These points are for conversation. They are not a spray schedule. Send growers to their university or KVK for product, dose and timing. Farmer how-to material belongs on our grower site.
what-to-tell-growers
What to tell growers, and what never to say

Safe to say:

  • Flowering depends on cool weather, mature shoots and last season's crop load.
  • Inputs can support a healthy tree. They cannot create a flowering season.
  • Try a new input on a few trees first and keep the comparison honest.
  • Results vary with soil, water, weather and management.

Never say:

  • "This will bring flowers" or "this stops fruit drop."
  • Any yield, income or disease-control figure.
  • That a biostimulant replaces pest or disease control.
  • That a date is certain.

Expect questions about paclobutrazol. Do not treat it as a shortcut at the counter. An IIHR study on Alphonso at Bengaluru, using soil drenches, found its residual influence persisted for three years after application stopped. A season's decision can carry into later seasons, so send that grower to a university horticulturist.

faq: When should a Gujarat dealer stock for mango flowering?
In tranches, not one lot. At one Valsad site, flowering began in early December one year and January the next. Take a small first lot now and tie the reorder to panicles seen in your own territory.
Should dealers give growers a mango spray schedule?
No. Share the stages and the risks, and send growers to their university or KVK for product, dose and timing. Bulletins change with the season and the place.
Can I sell biostimulant stock made under an old provisional certificate?

The September 2025 government release says provisional registrations stand invalid since 17 June 2025, but it does not address existing stock. Hold doubtful lots and check with your state agriculture department.
Will seaweed extract make mango trees flower?

No one can promise that. Flowering depends on cool weather, shoot maturity and crop load. Studies have looked at seaweed extract and fruit retention in specific trials, which are not a promise for any product.
Why do flowering dates shift so much between seasons?
Most mango cultivars need cool temperatures to flower, shoots need time to mature, and a heavy fruit load can inhibit flowering the next winter. Post-monsoon flushes can delay flowering further.
